To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in ABMR the resonance shifts due to inhomogeneous fields are proportional to the resonance width and that they are determined by a single parameter, the resonance frequency.

the frequency shifts of the NMR resonance line due to the inhomogeneities in the applied magnetic field and rf-field can be determined by measuring the line width of the NMR spectrum and that the shifts due to neighbouring states can be calculated by the theory.
the frequency of a resonance is not a constant but a variable that depends on the details of the experimental set-up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and the experimental realization of methods to determine the resonance frequency with an accuracy of a few 10 −9.
precision experiments in atomic and molecular physics and with the development of methods to determine the parameters of the atomic and molecular structure.
precision experiments in the field of atomic physics and quantum optics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resonance shifts due to the inhomogeneities can be neglected if they are small compared with the width of the resonance line.

all effects of field inhomogeneities can be reduced to a few simple terms, the most important ones being the shift due to the inhomogeneous rf-field, the shift due to a small inhomogeneity of B0 and the shift due to neighbouring states.

the ABMR method is a very powerful and precise technique for the measurement of magnetic moments, provided that one knows the line shape of the resonance curve and that the magnetic and the rf-field are homogeneous within the experimental errors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the last years we were able to reduce the uncertainty of the magnetic moment of the muonium ground state from 10−5 to 10−7.
we have developed a theory which is able to treat the influence of all possible inhomogeneities on the resonance frequency.
the ABMR technique has been developed to an accuracy of about 10-5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to determine the frequency shift due to an inhomogeneous magnetic field without a detailed knowledge about the line shape of the resonance.
in precision measurements the inhomogeneities in the experimental setup must be minimized to a level where the corresponding frequency shifts can be neglected.
one can find the shifts without a priori knowledge of the line shape.
